correctness.rationale: For a word with count vector \(k\), each coordinate edit can remove at most one surplus and one deficit, so its minimum Hamming distance to the target type class is exactly \(\frac12\sum_x|k_x-m_x|\). This gives the universal coupling lower bound. Conversely, repair exactly the surplus coordinates into deficits using a coordinate-permutation-equivariant random kernel. Since the product input law is exchangeable and the repaired output lies on the single coordinate-permutation orbit of the type class, the output is uniform; the coupling therefore attains the lower bound. The variance/Cauchy--Schwarz bounds and multinomial CLT with uniform integrability give the finite and asymptotic formulas. Independent full optimal-transport linear programs for several binary/ternary small types reproduced the identity, and the balanced binary formula follows from the standard central binomial absolute-deviation identity. The quantum inequality follows by the cited local preparation-channel contraction, with equality for orthogonal signal states.

originality.rationale: Originality passes. Girardi--De Palma--Lami prove the same type-class-to-product approximation only with normalized upper bound \(\sqrt{(N-1)\log(n+1)/(2n)}\), and their remark heuristically predicts Hamming displacement of order \(\sqrt n\). The audited equivariant repair coupling identifies the exact optimum, removes the logarithm, and gives the sharp fixed-type asymptotic constant. Constant-composition distribution matching studies different divergences/rate loss, and the quantum Wasserstein source supplies only the metric/data-processing framework.
